v1.0.0.changelog: Initial model training and local inference pipeline deployment.

spec.overview: An edge-deployed machine learning system performing real-time anomaly detection and predictive maintenance on motor vibration and temperature sensors.
spec.architecture: Utilizes a Python-based preprocessing and feature engineering pipeline, classical ML classifiers trained offline, and lightweight local inference engines deployed without cloud reliance.

subsystems.name: Preprocessing Pipeline
subsystems.function: Extracts statistical feature sets (mean, RMS, kurtosis) from raw sensor streams using sliding windows.

subsystems.name: ML Inference Core
subsystems.function: Classifies motor status as normal, alert, or critical using optimized Random Forest estimators.

subsystems.name: Edge Deploy Node
subsystems.function: Runs local anomaly validation cycles directly on sensor controller boards, bypassing network delays.

spec.challenges: Faced severe memory and processor limits when attempting to compute FFT frequency conversions on local edge microcontrollers.
spec.engineeringDecisions: Shifted anomaly features from frequency domains to time domains (root-mean-square and peak-to-peak amplitude metrics), achieving 88% precision with a 90% reduction in CPU cycles.
spec.lessonsLearned: Offline model training must replicate the specific coordinate limits and noise characteristics of real-world physical sensors.
spec.futureImprovements: Port model weights into C headers using micro-tensor toolkits to support ultra-low-power microcontrollers.

interviewQuestions.q: Why did you choose classical ML over Deep Learning (like LSTM) for anomaly detection?
interviewQuestions.a: Deep learning models require high memory capacities and floating-point acceleration. Classical Random Forest models achieved 88% precision while using less than 50KB of memory, which fits directly on edge microcontrollers without network delays.

replay.title: Data Pipeline Engineering
replay.description: Cleaned noisy sensor data streams and built coordinate sliding window systems.
replay.decisions: Used pandas to handle large test CSV matrices offline before porting equations.
replay.challenges: Irregular sampling rates from raw hardware sensors.
replay.lessons: Resampling sensor readings to a fixed frequency grid prevents model prediction biases.

replay.title: Model Training & Tuning
replay.description: Trained and evaluated classical ML models on vibration and heat targets.
replay.decisions: Selected Random Forest classifier over SVM due to better threshold control capabilities.
replay.challenges: Severe class imbalance (anomalies represent only 2% of raw data).
replay.lessons: Using synthetic oversampling techniques (SMOTE) balanced precision and recall scores.

replay.title: Edge Inference Porting
replay.description: Exported model weight arrays into optimized edge Python routines.
replay.decisions: Implemented inference using pure numpy logic to avoid importing heavy scikit-learn libraries.
replay.challenges: Throttled clock speeds on edge microcontrollers.
replay.lessons: Pre-computing math constants speeds up real-time sensor predictions.
